The African Democratic Congress has threatened to take its campaign rally to the streets of Kaduna following the state government’s refusal to grant it access to the Ranchers Bees Stadium for its scheduled November 17–18 activities. The opposition party accused the Kaduna State Government of using public facilities to frustrate its political activities, questioning why it was denied access to a stadium recently used by the ruling All Progressives Congress for its presidential campaign flag-off. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said the party had applied to the state government for permission to use the facility but was turned down by the Ministry of Local Government in a letter dated November 12. The ministry reportedly attributed the refusal to ongoing repair work at the stadium. However, the ADC questioned the explanation, noting that the APC had held its presidential campaign flag-off at the same venue on October 24, less than a month before the opposition party’s scheduled rally. This was the same stadium where the APC flagged off its presidential campaign on October 24. But we know what they are afraid of,” the party said. It alleged that the ruling party was uncomfortable with the large crowds attending its rallies across the North and did not want Kaduna residents to compare its political support with that of the opposition. The ADC insisted that the denial of access to the stadium would not stop its planned activities in the state, declaring its readiness to hold a street rally if the government refused to reconsider its decision. “If the Kaduna State Government will not allow us to campaign peacefully in the stadium, we will exercise our constitutional right to assemble peacefully in the streets. You may deny us a venue, but you cannot deny Nigerians their constitutional right to peaceful assembly,” the statement said. The party maintained that public facilities should be accessible to all political parties, regardless of their affiliations, arguing that denying opposition groups access to such infrastructure undermined the principle of a level playing field. It further urged the Kaduna State Government to reconsider its position, citing the Bauchi and Yobe state governments as examples of administrations it said had provided a more accommodating environment for opposition political activities. “If the APC government in Kaduna insists on closing public facilities to us, it would be violating the rights of its citizens to peaceful assembly and democratic choice. But our right to campaign in Kaduna or any other part of the country cannot be exercised at the discretion of a state governor,” the party said. The development comes amid growing political tensions as parties intensify preparations for the 2027 general elections, with access to public facilities for political campaigns emerging as a point of contention between opposition groups and some state governments.
